checks.name: routes-and-role-gates
checks.summary: A9, PASSED. POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:request-input and POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:answer-input are routed in the POST switch's default branch by prefix plus suffix, following the /v1/leases/{lease_id}:renew and /v1/executions/{execution_id}:start idiom, with the prefix and both suffixes as named constants. Role gates measured over HTTP: the ask is 401 unauthenticated, 403 for the owner, 200 for a Runner and 200 for the scheduler; the answer is 401 unauthenticated, 403 for a Runner, 403 for the scheduler and 200 for the owner. Every refusal is asserted to leave the Requirement's status and version unchanged. Both responses are checked against a CLOSED key allowlist and carry no key this Work Order did not name. A body carrying default_option is a 400 (the decoder already calls DisallowUnknownFields), so the transport cannot be talked into a default answer either. The detail response is scanned for the four forbidden name fragments (password, credential, raw_prompt, raw_provider_output) and contains none, and an unanswered question's needs_input object is asserted to carry none of answered_at, answered_option_id or answered_by.

checks.name: prefixes-are-not-swallowed
checks.summary: A9's routing clause, PASSED. The pre-existing /v1/requirements/ prefix branch is gated on r.Method == http.MethodGet, so a POST falls through to the verb branches; the proof asserted is behavioural rather than structural -- the POST to :request-input changes the stored Requirement to needs-input, which a read handler could not do. A POST to the bare detail path is 404 rather than being routed to a verb, and an empty requirement id before either suffix is 404. The same test asserts contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml declares both new literal path keys and the NeedsInputQuestion schema, and that the capability's declared owner_surfaces entry /v1/requirements/{requirement_id} is still declared.

checks.name: owner-console
checks.summary: A11, PASSED. See the web record for the additive-only measurement; this check is the assertion that runs it. The rendered console carries all ten new element ids and the V2-065 marker, and every pre-existing surface (capture, control, queue, repository, Release evidence, release-conditions, backlog-rows, runners-rows, providers-waiting, captured-rows) is still present. The owner.js block renders named rows rather than raw JSON, references none of http://, https://, //cdn, importScripts, setInterval, setTimeout or @font-face, and carries neither 'credential' nor 'raw_provider_output'. The submit control starts disabled and the answer call is bound to its onclick, so nothing submits an answer without an explicit owner action. The rendered markup contains no at-sign and none of password, secret, api_key, apikey, 'bearer ', 'authorization:' or private_key, and neither the markup nor the script carries either of the two prohibited overclaim phrases -- the one asserting that a capability was exercised, and the one asserting that a Preview journey passed -- which the same test checks for by name.
